senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. רָשָׁה) [to be powerful,] to do violence, be wicked.
units: <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 976:4">Yalk. Koh. 976</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Ecclesiastes 7:17">Koh. VII, 17</cite>) <he>אלא אם רָשַׁעְתָּ אל תִּרְשַׁע הרבה</he> (omitted in <cite ref="Shabbat 31b:5">Sabb. 31ᵇ</cite>) but it means, if thou hast once done wrong, do not therefore do more wrong.

senses.gloss: to declare in the wrong, to condemn.
units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 10a:11">Snh. 10ᵃ</cite> <he>אלא מעתה והצדיקו שנים והִרְשִׁיעוּ שנים וכ׳</he> if this be so (that you can derive from <he>ושפטום</he>, <cite ref="Deuteronomy 25:1">Deut. XXV, 1</cite>, that there must be two judges and one in addition to make a majority vote possible) then ‘and they shall justify’ (<cite ref="Deuteronomy 25:1">ib.</cite>) indicates two, ‘and they shall condemn’ (<cite ref="Deuteronomy 25:1">ib.</cite>) means two, hence you would require seven judges for a court!

senses.gloss: to charge with wrong-doing, accuse. Ib. עדים שהרשיעו את הצדיק וכ׳ if (false) witnesses accused an innocent person, and other witnesses came and justified him.
units: <cite ref="Bava Kamma 64b:12">B. Kam. 64ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Exodus 22:8">Ex. XXII, 8</cite>) <he>ולא המַרְשִׁיעַ עצמו</he> “he whom the judges shall condemn shall pay double”, but not he who accuses himself.

Ib. (ref. to Ex. XXII, 3) פרט למרשיע וכ׳ to the exemption of him who &c.; a. fr.— to do wrong. Tanḥ. D’barim 3; Yalk. Deut. 805 (play on רשעתים, Jud. III, 8) הם הרשיעו עלינו שתי רשעיות they (the Aramæans) did us two wrongs.
